name: Tha
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Adelberger, Jörg & Roger Blench. 2026. The peopling of the Muri Mountains, Northern Nigeria: evidence from linguistics and ethnography. AAeO - Afrikanistik-Aegyptologie-Online. doi:10.18716/OJS/AAEO/2026_12031
sources.note: Ethnohistory; Tha in Table 1 (Bikwin-Jen) and §4.3 p. 32 ('One group, the Tha, crossed the river and settled on the opposite bank'). No phonology; 'stress' only in the non-linguistic sense.
Stub: Tha (θá), Adamawa language of Taraba State, 1,000 speakers (1998); cites Ethnologue 18, Kleinewillinghöfer 2015, Adelberger & Blench 2026. Nothing on prosody.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 2020. Adamawa. In Rainer Vossen & Gerrit J. Dimmendaal (eds.), The Oxford Handbook of African Languages, 220-230. Oxford: Oxford University Press
sources.note: Family overview by the Bikwin-Jen fieldworker; Glottolog cites p. 224 for Tha's classification; may include typological notes on Adamawa prosody (tone) but a Tha-specific stress statement is improbable.
sources.venue: The Oxford Handbook of African Languages

sources.citation: Norton, Russell & Nlabephee Othaniel. 2020. The Jen language cluster: A comparative analysis of wordlists. Language in Africa 1(3): 17-99. doi:10.37892/2686-8946-2020-1-3-17-99
sources.note: Comparative phonology of ten Jen varieties incl. Tha (Joole Manga; Table 1 p. 18 autonym [ðə̀]). §3 treats vowels, nasalisation, tone (§3.3 pp. 43-45: 'High, mid, low, falling and rising tones were noted'; Table 20 p. 45 gives Tha reflexes *L>L, *H nouns>H,L, *H verbs>H, *M>M?), breathy voice, consonants. The words stress/accent occur 0 times; nothing on word stress.

sources.citation: Norton, Russell (& Nlabephee Othaniel). 2019. The Jen cluster: comparative analysis of wordlists. Slides, 1st Adamawa Conference, Mainz, 9-11 Sept 2019
sources.note: Lexicostatistics, vowel and consonant correspondence tables with a Tha column (tone-marked forms); no prose on tone or stress.

sources.citation: Othaniel, Nlabephee Kefas. 2017. A phonological comparative study of the Jen language cluster. BA research project, Theological College of Northern Nigeria, Bukuru / University of Jos (supervisor Russell Norton), 68 pp. (Glottolog 551275 lists it as an MA thesis, 83 pp.)
sources.note: §3.5 (pp. 21-22): Tha (ðə̀) data collected at Joole Manga; Joole Nyawo still speak a Dza dialect. §4.1 Table 3 (pp. 25-26) Tha consonant inventory (has ð, θ, ɟ, ʔ); §4.2-4.3 cognate sets and segmental correspondences on tone-marked 300-item wordlists. No tone or prosody section; stress/accent = 0 hits. (Copied from, originally downloaded fromhttps://llacan.cnrs.fr/AdaGram/publications/JEN_Jen_Language_Cluster_NLABEPHEE_2017_BA_thesis.pdf)

sources.venue: Adamawa Languages Project, JGU Mainz, 1 p

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2012. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 3rd ed. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. Entries 431 'Tha' and 220 'Joole'
sources.note: Index entry only: Tha, Taraba State (Karim Lamido LGA) and Adamawa State (Numan LGA), Joole Manga Dìdí village, Adamawa: Jen group, source Kleinewillinghöfer (1995). No phonology.

sources.note: Classification: 'Tha [Ɵá] spoken by the westernmost Joole group appears to be a distinct language.' Nothing on tone or stress.
sources.venue: Adamawa Languages Project web page, JGU Mainz
